key_insight: Ω-QVLA shows that vision-language-action models can be quantized more aggressively than previously thought, including the diffusion-based action head, without sacrificing stability. The key idea is to combine composite rotation with per-step scaling to make uniform quantization practical for end-to-end VLA deployment.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the high memory and compute cost of large VLA models, especially when deploying on-device. It tackles the long-standing challenge that the DiT action head was considered too unstable for uniform quantization, forcing prior methods to keep it in higher precision.
method: Apply composite rotation to improve the quantizability of the model’s representations and reduce sensitivity to low-bit precision.
Use per-step scaling to adapt quantization dynamically across diffusion steps in the action head.
Enable more uniform quantization across both the LLM backbone and the diffusion-based action module, instead of relying on mixed-precision workarounds.
impact: For practitioners, this means lower deployment cost, smaller memory footprint, and better feasibility for real-time or edge VLA systems. It also broadens the path toward fully quantized multimodal control policies rather than only compressing the language backbone.

paper_title: Ω-QVLA: Robust Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models via Composite Rotation and Per-step Scaling
paper_authors: Xinyu Wang, Mingze Li, Sicheng Lyu, Dongxiu Liu, Kaicheng Yang
